process_area.title: Haul-Away, Old-Unit Recycling, Reverse Logistics & Analytics

value_stream.name: Bulky & White-Goods Delivery, Installation, Haul-Away & Recycling Operations

fields.Participants: Ecommerce (VS-10), Trade (VS-11), Customer Service (VS-13), Compliance (VS-114), HSE (VS-24)
fields.Trigger: Bulky order with haul-away-eligible item (W4292); customer requests haul-away
fields.Volume: Haul-away-eligible orders (appliances, large furniture) × opt-in rate

workflows.name: Old-Appliance Haul-Away Policy, Eligibility & Customer Consent

Automation Opportunity: - Haul-away opt-in at checkout; consent + condition e-capture; manifest auto-inclusion; eligibility-rule engine
Controls: - CTL-661 (ensure controlled execution — Haul-Away, Old-Unit Recycling, Reverse Logistics & Analytics (PA-143.3).)
- CTL-661: haul-away consent captured & verified on-site; eligibility enforced; data-clearing on data-bearing devices (VS-91)
Cross-references: - links to VS-10/VS-16 (order), VS-114 (compliance), VS-25 (sustainability), VS-91 (data clearing), W4297 (manifest), W4308 (reverse logistics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unauthorized-removal risk**: crew hauls a unit not covered by consent → customer dispute/theft allegation; mitigated by consent capture + on-site verification
- **Condition-rejection risk**: customer expects haul-away of a unit outside policy (biohazard/oversized); mitigated by clear eligibility + in-app condition check
Time Estimate: - Policy ~2 weeks annual; per-order capture ~3 min; on-site haul-away ~10–15 min

steps.activity: Commercial/Sustainability set the haul-away policy — eligibility (1-for-1 on like-category new purchase), accepted condition, exclusions (e.g. biohazard/heavily-infested, oversized non-appliance), fee/subsidy, and customer-consent/data-clearing requirement
Order capture offers haul-away at purchase (VS-10/VS-11), captures customer consent + item description (type/age/condition, refrigerant flag), and books it onto the delivery manifest (W4297)
Crew execute haul-away at delivery (W4298) — verify the old unit matches consent, ensure data-bearing devices are data-cleared per consent, and load for reverse logistics (W4308)

fields.Participants: Licensed Installer (W4293), DENR-accredited recycler, Compliance (VS-114), ESG (VS-25), Risk (VS-21.2)
fields.Trigger: Haul-away of refrigerant-bearing appliance (refrigerator, freezer, AC, water cooler)

workflows.name: Refrigerant Recovery, ODS/RA 8749 & DENR-Compliant Appliance Handling

Automation Opportunity: - Refrigerant-recovery record app; auto chain-of-custody to accredited recycler; ESG ODS-recovery reporting
Controls: - CTL-81 (ensure bulky delivery compliance & e-POD closure.)
- CTL-661: refrigerant recovered not vented (RA 8749); licensed handler (W4293); accredited-recycler routing; chain-of-custody retained
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-114 (DG/compliance), VS-25 (ESG), VS-21.2 (risk), W4293 (license), W4307 (recycling), W4308 (reverse)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Venting risk**: refrigerant vented at removal → RA 8749 violation, fines, environmental harm; mitigated by recovery-equipment mandate + licensed handler (W4293) + accredited-recycler routing
- **Chain-of-custody risk**: recovered unit untraceable → compliance/ESG reporting failure; mitigated by tagged chain-of-custody record to accredited recycler

steps.activity: HSE/Compliance set the ODS (ozone-depleting substance / RA 8749 Clean Air Act) handling standard — recover (not vent) refrigerant at removal, use certified recovery equipment, route only to DENR-accredited recyclers
Licensed crew/recovery-tech recover refrigerant on removal (split-AC de-install, fridge compressor), label/tag the recovered charge, and document quantity/type
Compliance/ESG verify the recovered unit + refrigerant is delivered to a DENR-accredited recycler (W4307/W4308), retain the chain-of-custody record, and report ODS recovery for ESG (VS-25)

fields.Participants: Reverse Logistics (VS-32), DENR-accredited recycler/vendor, Compliance (VS-114), ESG (VS-25), Finance (VS-17.4)
fields.Trigger: Hauled-away old units consolidated for disposition

Automation Opportunity: - Disposition decision-tree by type/condition; recovery-value tracking; ESG landfill-diversion auto-report
Controls: - CTL-661 (ensure controlled execution — Haul-Away, Old-Unit Recycling, Reverse Logistics & Analytics (PA-143.3).)
- CTL-661: e-waste to DENR-accredited recycler; disposition classified; recovery/diversion documented (VS-25)
Cross-references: - links to VS-32 (reverse), VS-73 (waste/recycle), VS-114 (compliance), VS-25 (ESG), W4306 (refrigerant), W4310 (economics), W4311 (refurb)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-disposal risk**: e-waste to non-accredited channel → DENR/RA 6969 violation; mitigated by classification + accredited-recycler routing
- **Value-leak risk**: refurb/resale-eligible units scrapped → lost recovery; mitigated by disposition classification (W4311)
System Touchpoints: - Reverse logistics (VS-32); waste/recycle (VS-73); compliance (VS-114); ESG (VS-25); finance (VS-17.4); vendor (VS-03)

steps.activity: Reverse Logistics/Sustainability classify each hauled unit for disposition — refurb/resale (W4311), parts-harvest, scrap-metal recovery, e-waste (RA 6969/DENR), or responsible disposal — by type/condition
Reverse Logistics route to the right channel — accredited e-waste recycler (DENR), scrap-metal partner, refurb partner — and process via W4308 consolidation
ESG/Finance capture recovery value (scrap/refurb/parts), disposal cost, and the recycling/landfill-diversion outcome for ESG reporting (VS-25) and program economics (W4310)

fields.Participants: DC Ops (VS-04), Store Ops (VS-07), Reverse Logistics (VS-32), Scrap/Recycler Vendor, 3PL (VS-56), Finance (VS-17.4)
fields.Trigger: Hauled units at DC/store ready for consolidation

workflows.name: Haul-Away Reverse Logistics, Consolidation & Vendor Scrap Partner

Automation Opportunity: - Reverse-staging scan vs haul-away record; partner pickup scheduling; settlement auto-reconcile to GL
Controls: - CTL-661 (ensure controlled execution — Haul-Away, Old-Unit Recycling, Reverse Logistics & Analytics (PA-143.3).)
- CTL-661: record-vs-staging verification; chain-of-custody handoff; partner settlement reconciled (VS-17)
Cross-references: - links to VS-04 (DC), VS-32 (reverse), VS-56 (3PL), VS-03 (vendor), VS-17 (GL), W4305 (records), W4307 (disposition)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Reconciliation risk**: hauled units not matched to records → leakage/unaccounted disposal; mitigated by record-vs-staging verification + weigh/count handoff
- **Cost-leakage risk**: reverse-leg cost untracked → economics distortion; mitigated by partner settlement reconciliation to GL

steps.activity: DC/Store Ops consolidate hauled units at the designated reverse-staging area, verify against haul-away records (W4305), and stage by disposition (W4307)
steps.r: DC Ops / Store Ops / Reverse Logistics

steps.activity: Reverse Logistics/Vendor schedule the consolidator/scrap-metal/e-waste partner pickup or 3PL reverse-leg, with chain-of-custody handoff and weigh/count verification
Finance/Reverse Logistics reconcile partner settlement (scrap value, e-waste fee), post recovery/cost to the GL (VS-17), and close the reverse leg

fields.Participants: Compliance (VS-22/VS-114), ESG (VS-25), Legal (VS-100.3), DENR-accredited recyclers, Audit (VS-21)

Automation Opportunity: - Auto-aggregate haul-away/recycling records into EPR report; chain-of-custody archival; DENR submission workflow
Controls: - CTL-81 (ensure bulky delivery compliance & e-POD closure.)
- CTL-661: EPR (RA 11898) record complete; chain-of-custody to accredited processor; records retained (VS-88)
Cross-references: - links to VS-22/VS-114 (compliance), VS-25 (ESG), VS-88 (records), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-21 (audit), W4306 (refrigerant), W4310 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Reporting-gap risk**: incomplete EPR record → DENR/RA 11898 non-compliance, fines; mitigated by complete chain-of-custody documentary trail
- **Audit-trail risk**: records missing/disposed early; mitigated by retention policy (VS-88) and accredited-processor proof retention
System Touchpoints: - Compliance/permits (VS-22); DG/compliance (VS-114); ESG (VS-25); records (VS-88); legal (VS-100.3); audit (VS-21)
Time Estimate: - ~2–3 weeks annual EPR compilation; record-keeping continuous

steps.activity: Compliance/ESG map BuildRight's EPR (RA 11898 Extended Producer Responsibility) obligations for end-of-life appliances/e-waste and the documentary trail required (quantity, type, chain-of-custody, accredited-processor proof)

Compliance/Sustainability compile the EPR/recycling record (haul-away quantities, refrigerant recovery W4306, e-waste to accredited recycler W4307, recovery/diversion W4310) and submit required reports to DENR/EMB
Audit/Legal verify the documentary trail, retain records per policy (VS-88), and respond to any DENR/audit inquiry

fields.Participants: Finance (VS-17.4), Sustainability (VS-25), Reverse Logistics, Revenue Assurance (VS-118), Procurement (VS-34)
fields.Trigger: Operating performance; finance close; sustainability review

Automation Opportunity: - Per-unit haul-away/recycling economics dashboard; RA leakage detection; ESG diversion/CO₂e auto-calc
Controls: - CTL-661 (ensure controlled execution — Haul-Away, Old-Unit Recycling, Reverse Logistics & Analytics (PA-143.3).)
- CTL-661: full per-unit economics tracked; leakage RA-monitored (VS-118); diversion reported (VS-25)
Cross-references: - links to VS-17.4 (finance), VS-118 (revenue assurance), VS-25 (ESG), VS-32/VS-73 (reverse/waste), W4295 (fees), W4311 (refurb)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hidden-cost risk**: reverse-leg/processing cost unallocated → net economics mis-stated; mitigated by full per-unit P&L
- **Value-leak risk**: scrap/refurb value not captured; mitigated by recovery-value tracking & RA monitoring
System Touchpoints: - Finance/GL (VS-17.4); revenue assurance (VS-118); ESG (VS-25); reverse logistics (VS-32/VS-73); procurement (VS-34)

steps.activity: Finance/Sustainability track the full haul-away/recycling P&L — haul-away fee revenue (W4295), scrap/refurb/parts recovery value, refrigerant/e-waste processing cost, reverse-leg cost (W4308), and net per-unit economics
Revenue Assurance/Finance detect leakage (under-billed haul-away fee, un-recovered scrap value, inflated processing cost) and recover
Sustainability/Finance report landfill-diversion tonnes, CO₂e-avoided, and recovery rate, and feed improvement to W4307/W4311 and ESG (VS-25)

fields.Participants: Reverse Logistics (VS-32), Quality (VS-31), Refurb Partner, Clearance (VS-64), Finance (VS-17.4), LP (VS-23)
fields.Trigger: Hauled unit or customer-return assessed as refurb/resale-eligible
fields.Volume: Refurb/resale-eligible units (subset of hauled-away + VS-32 returns)

workflows.name: Bulky Reverse-Logistics Asset Recovery, Refurb/Open-Box & Liquidation

Automation Opportunity: - Refurb-eligibility scoring; recovery-vs-scrap analytics; refurb-disclosure auto-label; LP exception monitoring
Controls: - CTL-661 (ensure controlled execution — Haul-Away, Old-Unit Recycling, Reverse Logistics & Analytics (PA-143.3).)
- CTL-661: refurb safety-assessed & disclosed; recovery tracked; LP-monitored (VS-23); data cleared (VS-91)
Cross-references: - links to VS-32 (reverse), VS-31 (quality), VS-64 (clearance), VS-23 (LP), VS-91 (privacy), W4307 (disposition), W4310 (economics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unsafe-resale risk**: unsafe/uncertified refurbished unit resold → safety/Consumer Act (RA 7394) exposure; mitigated by refurb eligibility/safety assessment + disclosure
- **Diversion risk**: refurb-eligible units diverted to scrap/personal gain; mitigated by LP monitoring (VS-23) & recovery tracking
System Touchpoints: - Reverse logistics (VS-32); quality (VS-31); clearance (VS-64); finance (VS-17.4); LP (VS-23); privacy (VS-91)

steps.activity: Reverse Logistics/Quality assess each candidate unit for refurb/resale eligibility (cosmetic vs functional, safety, warranty/legality of resale, data-bearing clearing VS-91) per VS-32.3
Reverse Logistics route eligible units — in-house/partner refurb, certified-refurb relabel, open-box liquidation via VS-64 channels, or parts-harvest — and price for recovery
Finance/LP track recovery vs scrap-baseline, ensure resale compliance (refurb disclosure, no resale of unsafe/counterfeit), and prevent leak/diversion

fields.Participants: Commercial (VS-01), CX (VS-13), Finance (VS-17.4), Sustainability (VS-25), HSE (VS-24), Strategy (VS-33)

workflows.name: Bulky Delivery/Install/Recycle Program Performance & Sustainability Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - Integrated program-KPI dashboard; circular-economy flow visualization; ESG auto-feed; benchmark analytics
Controls: - CTL-661 (ensure controlled execution — Haul-Away, Old-Unit Recycling, Reverse Logistics & Analytics (PA-143.3).)
- CTL-661: program KPIs reviewed quarterly; improvement actions prioritized; ESG outcome reported (VS-25)
Cross-references: - links to VS-06 (logistics), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-25 (ESG), VS-13 (CX), VS-33 (strategy), VS-36/VS-21 (governance), W4296 (delivery analytics), W4310 (economics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Sub-optimization risk**: delivering on delivery-SLA while recycling economics degrade; mitigated by integrated program-KPI view
- **Narrative-gap risk**: strong circular-economy outcome not reflected in ESG narrative; mitigated by consolidated sustainability reporting
System Touchpoints: - Logistics analytics (VS-06); finance (VS-17.4); ESG (VS-25); CX (VS-13); strategy (VS-33); governance (VS-36/VS-21)
Time Estimate: - Quarterly review ~2–3 days; annual report ~1–2 weeks

steps.a: Head of Bulky Delivery / Sustainability Lead
steps.activity: Delivery Ops/Analytics consolidate program KPIs — on-time-window %, first-time-success %, install-complete %, damage %, haul-away completion %, recovery $/unit, landfill-diversion tonnes, CO₂e avoided, customer NPS
Commercial/Strategy benchmark vs cost-to-serve and competitor offering, identify improvement (capacity, install quality, recovery), and prioritize actions
Sustainability/Leadership report the bulky circular-economy outcome (haul-away→recycle→refurb) into the ESG/sustainability narrative (VS-25) and board assurance (VS-36/VS-21)
